newsitem.title: USA: US Tsy's Summers' tax remark not constructive-Lott.
newsitem.headline: US Tsy's Summers' tax remark not constructive-Lott.

text.p: A senior Treasury official's criticism of proponents of ending the estate tax was "not constructive" at a time when Congress and the White House are trying to forge a budget deal, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday.

"It is not constructive to have a sub-cabinet level official using the word 'selfish' to describe supporters of death tax reform at a time when we're trying to forge a bipartisan budget agreement with the President," Lott said in a statement.
Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers Monday accused opponents of the U.S. tax system of "selfishness" and of wanting to "whip Americans into a frenzy."
Summers said most tax cuts should benefit middle income Americans instead of the very wealthy and singled out supporters of an inheritance tax cut for special criticism.
"I hope that comments like this do not poison the well for getting a bipartisan agreement on balancing the budget and providing needed tax relief..." Lott, a Mississippi Republican, said.
